title: Get started with NMADTA
text: NMADTA needs R 4.0.0 later JAGS 4.x. JAGS separate program: install JAGS project first. rjags load, check JAGS installed operating system processor architecture, restart R.
code: install.packages("NMADTA") library(NMADTA) rjags::jags.version() packageVersion("NMADTA")

title: Get started with NMADTA
text: dat.kang dataset 48 rows joint outcome counts 12 studies. candidate tests D-dimer ultrasonography; venography reference. missing test indicated delta = 0 outcome code 999. rows record joint test outcomes, rather separate 2 2 table every comparison. Read Preparing data using study data.

title: Get started with NMADTA
text: nstu = 12 number studies K = 2 counts candidate tests, excluding reference standard. run uses 5,000 adaptation iterations, followed 50,000 iterations per chain, first 25,000 removed burn-. Three chains used. Running time depends model, data, computer.
code: set.seed(10) kang_fit <- nmadt.hierarchical(   nstu = 12, K = 2, data = dat.kang,   testname = c("D-dimer", "Ultrasonography"),   directory = tempdir(),   n.adapt = 5000, n.iter = 50000, n.chains = 3,   n.burnin = 25000, n.thin = 1,   conv.diag = TRUE, trace = NULL,   dic = FALSE, mcmc.samples = FALSE )

title: MNAR sensitivity analysis
text: nmadt.hierarchical.MNAR() extends hierarchical formulation. nmadt.hsroc.MNAR() extends HSROC formulation. input uses column structure regular fitting functions.

title: MNAR sensitivity analysis
text: gamma1 gamma0 numeric vectors length K. describe dependence missingness test sensitivity specificity, respectively, model’s logit scale. reference recommends treating sensitivity-analysis parameters. Zero represents dependence corresponding accuracy parameter; negative values can represent poorer-performing tests likely missing selection model.
code: library(NMADTA) data(dat.kang)  fit_mnar <- nmadt.hierarchical.MNAR(   nstu = 12, K = 2, data = dat.kang,   testname = c("D-dimer", "Ultrasonography"),   gamma1 = c(-0.5, -0.5),   gamma0 = c(-0.5, -0.5),   directory = tempdir(),   n.adapt = 5000, n.iter = 50000, n.chains = 3,   conv.diag = TRUE ) summary(fit_mnar)

title: MNAR sensitivity analysis
text: Repeat fit prespecified grid. grid value applied tests accuracy coefficients: values illustrate workflow. Choose plausible assumptions review, document , check convergence fit. observed data alone identify missingness mechanism. See reference complete arguments article examples.
code: gamma_grid <- c(0, -0.5, -1, -2) fits <- lapply(gamma_grid, function(g) {   nmadt.hierarchical.MNAR(     nstu = 12, K = 2, data = dat.kang,     testname = c("D-dimer", "Ultrasonography"),     gamma1 = rep(g, 2), gamma0 = rep(g, 2),     directory = tempdir(),     n.adapt = 5000, n.iter = 50000, n.chains = 3,     conv.diag = TRUE   ) }) names(fits) <- paste0("gamma_", gamma_grid) lapply(fits, summary)

title: Choosing a model
text: nmadt.hierarchical() directly models accuracy parameters, including sensitivity specificity, -study random effects. Pooled sensitivity specificity natural summary quantities. model described Ma, Lian, Chu, Ibrahim, Chen (2018), Biostatistics.
code: library(NMADTA) data(dat.kang)  fit <- nmadt.hierarchical(   nstu = 12, K = 2, data = dat.kang,   testname = c("D-dimer", "Ultrasonography") )

title: Choosing a model
text: nmadt.hsroc() uses accuracy threshold components. parameterization useful considering differences operating thresholds across studies comparisons across ROC space. model described Lian, Hodges, Chu (2019), Journal American Statistical Association.
code: fit_hsroc <- nmadt.hsroc(   nstu = 12, K = 2, data = dat.kang,   testname = c("D-dimer", "Ultrasonography"),   n.adapt = 5000, n.iter = 50000, n.chains = 3 )

K integer indicating number candiate test dataset. data list conating input dataset used meta-analysis. testname string vector names candidate tests dataset order presetned dataset. directory string specifying designated directory save trace plots potential scale reduction factors calculated function. default NULL. eta number indicating mean log(S) log(P) determines covariance matrices cutoff values accuracy values respectively. default 0. xi_preci number indicating precision log(S) log(P) determines covariance matrices cutoff values accuracy values respectively. default 1.25. digits positive integer number digits right decimal point keep results; digits=4 default. n.adapt positive integer indicating number iterations adaptation. default 5,000. n.iter postive integer indicating number iterations MCMC chain. default 50,000. n.chains postive interger indicating number MCMC chains. default 3. n.burnin positive integer indicating number burn-iterations beginning chain without saving posterior samples. default floor(n.iter/2). n.thin thinning rate MCMC chains, used save memory computation time n.iter large. example, algorithm saves one sample every nth iteration, n given n.thin. conv.diag logical value specifying whether compute potential scale reduction factors proposed convergence diagnostics. default FALSE. trace string vector containing subset different quantities can chosen prevalence("prev"), sensitivity ("Se"), specificity ("Sp"), positive negative predictive values ("ppv" "npv" repectively), positive likelihood ("LRpos"), negative likelihood ("LRneg"). dic logical value indicating whether function output deviance information criterion (DIC) statistic. default false. mcmc.samples logical value indicating whether coda samples generated meta-analysis. default FALSE.

text: x object class `nmadt`, typically produced one model-fitting functions: nmadt.hierarchical() — hierarchical model MAR assumption; nmadt.hsroc() — HSROC model MAR assumption; nmadt.hierarchical.MNAR() — hierarchical model allowing   MNAR (missing random) mechanism; nmadt.hsroc.MNAR() — HSROC model allowing MNAR mechanism. functions return object class `nmadt` suitable plotting. type Character string specifying type plot generate. One "sroc", "density", "forest", "contour". Defaults "sroc" specified. ... Additional arguments passed underlying plotting functions (e.g., graphical parameters cex.axis, cex.lab, etc.).

title: Plot method for `nmadt` objects — plot.nmadt
text: Invisibly returns input `nmadt` object x. function primarily called side effect generating plots rather returning value.

title: Plot method for `nmadt` objects — plot.nmadt
text: available plot types : "sroc" (default) Summary Receiver Operating Characteristic (SROC) curve.     Visualizes trade-sensitivity specificity     across studies, along hierarchical model fit. "density" Posterior density plots study- test-level sensitivity     specificity parameters.     Useful checking convergence posterior uncertainty. "forest" Forest plot summarizing point estimates uncertainty intervals     sensitivity specificity test across studies.     Helpful visualizing study heterogeneity. "contour" Contour-enhanced plots showing joint posterior density     sensitivity specificity test study.     Useful visual comparison test performance. type specified, function defaults "sroc". example, plot(x) plot(x, type = "sroc") produce SROC plot.
